meta.promptText: Which vitamin C serum should I buy for dark spots and dull skin in India?

response.text:
For **dark spots + dull skin**, I’d keep it simple and choose a **stable 10% vitamin C** rather than jumping straight to a very high concentration.

### My top picks in India

### [Minimalist Vitamin C 10% Face Serum]()
*₹284*

### [Deconstruct 10% Vitamin C Serum]()
*₹468*

### [Plum 15% Vitamin C Face Serum Mandarin]()
*₹456*

**1. Best overall for most people: Minimalist 10% Vitamin C**  
It uses **10% Ethyl Ascorbic Acid**, a relatively stable vitamin-C derivative, plus 1% Acetyl Glucosamine. It's fragrance-free and designed specifically for dullness, sun damage and dark spots. [beminimalist.co](https://beminimalist.co/collections/best-sellers/products/vitamin-c-ethyl-ascorbic-acid-10-acetyl-glucosamine-1?utm_source=chatgpt.com)  
**My pick if you're starting vitamin C.**

**2. Best value: Deconstruct 10% Vitamin C + 0.5% Ferulic Acid**  
This is a particularly nice option for pigmentation because it combines 10% vitamin C with **ferulic acid**, which helps stabilize and support antioxidant performance. It's also fragrance-free. [thedeconstruct.in](https://thedeconstruct.in/collections/shop/products/vitamin-c-and-ferulic-acid-serum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**3. For experienced users: Plum 15% Vitamin C**  
The higher 15% concentration makes more sense if you've already used vitamin C without irritation and want a stronger brightening product. [www.pingmedoc.com](https://www.pingmedoc.com/pharmacy/buying-guides/best-vitamin-c-serum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### What I'd buy
**Start with Minimalist 10%** if this is your first vitamin-C serum. If your skin is already accustomed to actives, **Deconstruct 10% + ferulic acid** is an excellent alternative.

**How to use:** 2–3 drops in the morning after cleansing → moisturizer → **SPF 50 sunscreen**. Sunscreen is crucial; otherwise, UV exposure can keep bringing pigmentation back. Consistent use generally takes **several weeks to a few months** to show meaningful improvement. [www.whowhatwear.com](https://www.whowhatwear.com/beauty/skin/best-products-for-hyperpigmentation?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

One important tip: if a vitamin-C serum turns **deep orange/brown**, it may have oxidized and is best replaced. [www.vogue.in](https://www.vogue.in/content/the-7-best-vitamin-c-serums-for-an-even-toned-complexion?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

If you tell me your **skin type (oily/dry/combination/sensitive), age, and budget (e.g. under ₹500/₹1000)**, I can narrow it down to **one exact serum** for you.

sources.snippet:
This article from Who What Wear UK provides a comprehensive guide to the best skincare products for treating hyperpigmentation, featuring insights from dermatologists and skin experts. Hyperpigmentation, a common skin concern caused by excess melanin, can result from sun exposure, hormonal changes (such as pregnancy-related melasma), inflammation, or acne scarring. The guide emphasizes that the cause of pigmentation determines the best treatment and underlines the importance of daily SPF use as the most critical step in both prevention and treatment.

Recommended ingredients include vitamin C, niacinamide, azelaic acid, tranexamic acid, and retinoids, which can be found in both over-the-counter and prescription products. Experts caution that results typically take 6 to 12 weeks, or even months, and consistency in skincare is essential.

The article highlights 13 carefully selected products, spanning cleansers, serums, moisturizers, and SPFs. Notable mentions include La Roche-Posay Mela B3 Cleanser, Eucerin Pigment Control SPF50+, The Ordinary Azelaic Acid 10%, and Murad Rapid Dark Spot Correcting Serum. Each product is chosen based on expert input, performance, ingredient quality, and user reviews, providing practical options for anyone tackling dark spots and uneven skin tone.
